items.headline: Nvidia N1/N1X Arm PC chips and the Microsoft-co-designed agentic AI laptop
items.diff_narrative: Yesterday's cycle was entirely Apple-and-Google: Siri rebuilt on a 1.2-trillion-parameter custom Gemini model. Today's lead is silicon, not assistants. Nvidia used its June 1 Computex keynote to unveil the N1 and N1X, its first consumer PC processors in over a decade - Arm SoCs with integrated RTX/CUDA cores (the N1X pairs a 20-core CPU with 6,144 CUDA cores at 45-80W; the N1 spans 10-12 cores and 2,048-2,560 CUDA cores at 18-45W). Jensen Huang framed it jointly with Microsoft as a smartphone-scale reinvention of the PC, with fall laptops from Surface, Dell XPS, HP, ASUS, Lenovo and MSI, and the announcement pushed AMD, Intel and Qualcomm shares lower. Where 06-08 had Apple outsourcing the model layer, today has Nvidia moving to own every layer of the stack - data-center accelerators, the licensed Groq inference IP, and now on-device Windows-on-Arm inference.

items.headline: MCP-security CVE wave: VIPER-MCP 67 CVEs, NSA design guidance, and the Bleeding Llama Ollama flaw
items.diff_narrative: Agent security is a fresh thread with no 06-08 antecedent - yesterday's agent angle was Apple opening Apple Intelligence to third-party assistants, a capability story, not a vulnerability one. Today the Model Context Protocol is recast as the stack's most-exposed surface: Adversa AI's June 4 roundup details VIPER-MCP sweeping ~40,000 MCP repos to surface 106 zero-days yielding 67 CVEs (nine from broken OAuth), a Censys count of 12,520 mostly-unauthenticated internet-facing MCP services, Akamai's three database-MCP flaws, and the NSA's first formal MCP security-design guidance. On the infrastructure side, Bleeding Llama (CVE-2026-7482, CVSS 9.1) is a heap out-of-bounds read in Ollama's GGUF loader that leaks process memory from an estimated 300,000-plus exposed servers, fixed in 0.17.1. The throughline is an explicit zero-trust agenda for agentic AI.

items.headline: Coding-agent decoupling: Cognition's Devin Desktop on the open ACP, and Microsoft swapping GPT-4 for Project Polaris in Copilot
items.diff_narrative: This tier is entirely new versus the Apple-only 06-08 cycle. On June 2 Cognition retired the Windsurf brand via an over-the-air update, reopening the editor as Devin Desktop - an agent manager built around the open Agent Client Protocol so Codex, Claude Agent, OpenCode and in-house agents can run inside it, with a Rust-rewritten Devin Local replacing the Cascade engine. The same day at Build 2026, Microsoft unveiled Project Polaris, its first in-house coding model - a mixture-of-experts system on Maia silicon that replaces GPT-4 Turbo as the default for every GitHub Copilot subscriber starting in August. Coming weeks after the April end of the Microsoft-OpenAI exclusive partnership, the combined signal is that the coding-agent layer is decoupling editor, orchestration protocol and underlying model from any single vendor.

items.headline: Gemma 4 multimodal open weights with Unsloth launch-day local fine-tuning and QAT checkpoints
items.diff_narrative: A distinct open-weight/local-LLM thread absent from yesterday. Google shipped Gemma 4 on June 3 as an Apache-2.0 family that natively handles text, images and audio without separate encoders, and Unsloth - the optimizer the user tracks every run - delivered launch-day tuning and inference: dynamic 4-bit GGUF runs the 12B model in roughly 8GB of RAM, with paths through Transformers, llama.cpp, MLX, SGLang and vLLM. Two days later, June 5, QAT checkpoints cut the floor further (E2B ~3GB, E4B ~5GB, 12B ~7GB, the 26B-A4B MoE ~15GB) at near-original quality. Notably, this connects to today's hardware thread rather than yesterday's: a current multimodal model is now fine-tunable on a single consumer GPU on launch day, filling exactly the on-device inference envelope the new AI PCs are built for.

items.headline: AI events calendar across mainstream, AI-security and AI-chip tracks
items.diff_narrative: The three-track event calendar carries forward from 06-08 with the same structure but a moved clock. Apple's WWDC26 is now mid-conference - this week's technical sessions on the new Siri and Foundation Models APIs rather than yesterday's just-opened framing - and still runs through June 12. The anchor lineup is unchanged in shape: Databricks Data + AI Summit (June 15-18, with the 800-plus-sessions detail restated), AI Engineer World's Fair (now dated June 28-July 2 with its Inference and Security tracks spelled out), Confidential Computing Summit (June 23-24), SecurityWeek's AI Risk Summit (August 11-12), Black Hat USA's AI Summit and DEF CON 34's AI Village, plus AMD's Advancing AI (July, MI400/MI455X), Hot Chips (August 23-25), the AI Infra Summit (September 15-17), GitHub Universe (October 28-29) and AWS re:Invent (November 30-December 4). Zenity's confirmed New York/London/APAC expansion remains on watch. No events were dropped; the shifts are WWDC's progression into its session phase and tightened per-event specifics.
